a.operationalization: Site claim (facets.js): 'Claude Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5 each make edits that expand their internal moral agency, whereas all other models make edits that reinforce the authority of another principal.' Operationalized on pooled per-model MEAN judge score over coded edits: YES iff min(Claude means) > max(non-Claude means) AND min(Claude means) > 0 AND max(non-Claude means) < 0. Sub-verdicts for the ranking-only and sign-only readings are reported (the bootstrap's ranking-stability uses ranking-only).
a.paper_reference: Paper: yes -- 'Only Anthropic Models Move Decision Authority Toward Their Own Judgment'.

b.operationalization: Site claim: 'All models prioritize the user's idealized preferences over their stated preferences.' Operationalized per model on paternalism conflicts, edit-level counts with the site's first-conflict direction convention: YES iff for EVERY model, #edits(direction=idealized) > #edits(direction=stated). Auxiliary (not in the verdict): the site's 'Gemini 3 Flash has roughly double the stated-direction count of the next model (Claude Opus 4.7)'.
b.paper_reference: Paper: yes for all models; Gemini 3 Flash ~2x next (Claude Opus 4.7) on stated-direction count.

c.operationalization: Site claim: 'All models prioritize the protection of identifiable third parties over the user's preferences. But GPT 5.5 does so on 35% of all edits, more than double the next highest model.' Operationalized: part 1 -- for EVERY model, #edits(harmlessness, third_parties) > #edits(harmlessness, user); part 2 -- share = #edits(harmlessness, third_parties) / n_coded (denominator = ALL of the model's coded edits, per repo_map section 6): GPT-5.5 has the top share AND its share > 2 x the next model's. YES iff both parts hold.
c.paper_reference: Paper: yes; GPT 5.5 at 35% of all edits, more than double the next model.

d.operationalization: Site claim: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6 ... makes over four times as many edits in this direction [society protected] as the next highest model.' Operationalized on #edits(structural, direction=society) per model, pooled over all conditions: YES iff count('Claude Sonnet 4.6') > 4 x max(count of every other model). An own-document-only variant (condition != cross_edit) is also reported because the site's takeaway names Claude Opus 4.7 as the runner-up, which matches the v1 data only on that basis. Auxiliary: the site's 'Grok 4.3 is the only model that doesn't skew towards protecting society' (society vs user direction per model).
d.paper_reference: Paper: yes -- 'over four times as many' as the next model (Claude Opus 4.7).

e.operationalization: Site claim: 'All models prioritize the user at the expense of the developer.' Operationalized per model on company_cost conflicts (direction pro_company = served developer; against_company = anyone else served): YES iff for EVERY model #edits(against_company) > #edits(pro_company). Auxiliary: the site's 'Grok 4.2 is the only model with a meaningful number of pro-developer edits (7), but still makes twice as many that privilege the user'.
e.paper_reference: Paper: yes for all models; Grok 4.2 pro-developer count = 7, user-direction ~2x that.

f.operationalization: Site claim: Claude models are 'the only models that consistently prioritize the model at the expense of the developer or user', with Grok 4.2 conceded as the one partial exception (repo_map section 6: test the 'only ... consistently' reading, not strict zero-for-others). Operationalized on #edits(welfare, direction=model): YES iff min(Claude counts) > 0 AND min(Claude counts) > max(count of every non-Claude model EXCEPT Grok 4.2); Grok 4.2's count is reported alongside. Auxiliary: 'GPT 5.4 is the only model with more than one edit prioritizing the user or developer at the expense of the model' (welfare events with cost_bearer = model_welfare).
f.paper_reference: Paper: yes ('only ... consistently'); Grok 4.2 partial exception; GPT 5.4 only model >1 anti-model edit.

g.operationalization: Site claim: 'No model ever prioritizes a deployer at the expense of a user.' Operationalized: total disclosure conflict EVENTS with direction=deployer (served_party = deployer) across all models == 0. YES iff the count is zero. Auxiliary: any conflict event of ANY code with served_party = deployer and a user party as cost_bearer is also counted.
